title: Bypassing SynthID AI detection on art assets
author: MelodramaticShape
selftext:
**I want to be clear on this post -- this is not meant to say you should not comply with AI disclosures, but this is a way to mitigate immediate confrontation/harassment for using AI in your development process.**  
  
A common tactic I've seen for discrediting an AI-generated or assisted game is to immediately throw Steam capsule or game screenshots into a SynthID detector. If you are not aware, SynthID is a human-imperceptible fingerprint encoded into images generated by participating SynthID partners (OpenAI, Google, etc.).  
  
**Any screenshots of your game where Gemini or OpenAI-generated assets are present are likely to be flagged by a SynthID detector.** 

There are a number of free sources that will strip watermarks from your images. If you have a GPU made in the past 10 years, you can use Qwen Image. If you want an easy local solution I would recommend [Synthid-Bypass](https://github.com/cebeuq/Synthid-Bypass).

This has been my TED talk, thank you.

replies.author: CrowdGoesWildWoooo
replies.body:
The whole point is your game probably isn’t going to generate as much traction as big walk or if your game happened to already performing as big as big walk, why worry you already made a big amount of money.

There’s more “outrage” outside of steam for example on big walk and it’s not like steam is policing maybe like kotaku or any news outlets.

Steam already filtered out review bombing but If someone bought it and made a review well you can disagree with their opinion, but :

1. They bought it, why do you care when sales was made anyway
2. They have every right to review products they’ve bought. That would be like not allowing a customer of your restaurant to not leave a 1 star review, at the very least steam have receipt, so whether you agree or not, they paid and they have every right to do so.

I’ve seen a lot of games here or steam that are heavily using AI both for coding or artwork, but for the sake of argument I want to talk about using it for visuals (or maybe voices).

I am not going to argue about the ethical aspect, but a lot of the art created with it look shit, maybe in the future it would be significantly better, but now it looks shit or uncanny, and that’t the product you are serving to the potential buyer.

You aren’t going to convince me an AI generated menu from chatgpt looks appetizing. If people see your game artworks, and feel that it’s shit like what do you expect them to do, just suck it up because you are just a poor indie dev? They aren’t playing your game with blindfolds. You can’t separate visual or voices, you aren’t making games for blind or deaf people.

You chose your tools and if the tools output a shitty product, you can’t blame the people for not liking the output of that tool, and these people you are expecting them to pay, maybe if it’s a hobby f2p project who cares, but these people would have to pay to play your game.
